style.title: Design system
style.intro: The colours, typefaces, motion and components of the site, gathered on one page to check them in light and dark, on phone and on computer.
style.colorsIntro: Two colours, those of the coat of arms: white and red. Everything else is ink and grey. The contrast ratio is measured against the page background.
style.typeIntro: Titles in Bodoni Moda, text in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. The ÿ must be perfectly drawn.
style.typeSample: A family, its faces, its stories
style.typeBody: Body text: 16 pixels on phones, 18 on computers. Short sentences in the narrative present, written for a cousin rather than a historian.
style.spacingIntro: White space breathes: wide margins, few elements per screen. Corners stay sharp, like the bands and the shield. Motion lasts 200 to 600 milliseconds.
style.motifIntro: The three bars become a separator, a loading indicator and the page transition; the two dots of the ÿ serve as bullet and marker.
style.cardExcerpt: Example text. The beginning of the story will show here, three lines at most, to make you want to read on.
style.fieldDateError: Enter at least the year, for example 1890.
style.fieldAnonymousHint: The administrator will know who wrote it.
style.panelIntro: On computers it slides in from the right; on phones it rises from the bottom of the screen.
style.panelBody: A person’s profile will open here from the tree: portrait, dates, marriages, parents and children, related stories.
style.armsIntro: Drawn for the site as crisp SVG. The family can replace them with its own files.
style.glossary: Every technical term is explained in one click: three <fasce>bars</fasce> <gueules>gules</gueules> on an <argent>argent</argent> field, a <ecartele>quartered</ecartele> shield, <doloire>doloires</doloire>.
style.emptyIntro: A section without content invites people to contribute: never a hole, never filler text.
style.menuFooterIntro: The menu is at the top of this page; the footer at the bottom. Below 1360 pixels wide, the menu opens full screen.

guide.title: Administrator’s guide
guide.intro: Two pages to keep the site running day to day. Nothing is published without you, and everything you do can be undone.

points.1: Delete the demonstration data: the « Exemple » family is fictional and goes in one click.
points.2: Follow “Getting started” on the overview: the arms, the home page summary, the first ancestors, the first photos, three cousins invited.
points.3: A tree already entered in genealogy software can be imported at once (Import and export, GEDCOM file). Nothing is written before you confirm.

points.1: The overview gathers what awaits your decision: suggestions, access requests, photos and stories to approve.
points.2: A suggestion is accepted or declined with a word for its author, who receives it by email. “Apply” opens the record’s form, already filled in, next to the current record.
points.3: Accepting “This is me” links a member’s account to their record in the tree.

points.1: People: one person in the centre, then “+” for a parent, a spouse or a child. A date can stay vague: “about 1450”, “1450”.
points.2: Stories and anecdotes: link them to the people concerned, and they appear on their records by themselves.
points.3: Photos: send several at once, then outline the faces and name them.
points.4: Places and events: a click on the map places a place; an event has a date, a place and people.
points.5: Arms and titles: your SVG files replace the site’s drawings.
points.6: On the site, the “Edit” button leads straight to the matching screen.

points.1: A person is treated as living as long as they have neither a date of death nor the “deceased” box ticked, unless they were born more than a hundred years ago.
points.2: A living person is never visible to the public or to search engines: the public tree shows “Living person”. Signed-in members see them.
points.3: Before publishing a photo or a story showing living people, ask for their consent.

points.1: Invite a cousin by email address: they receive a sign-in link valid for seven days.
points.2: Access requests sent from the Contribute page are accepted or declined here.
points.3: A member can become an administrator; an account can be disabled without being deleted.

points.1: The journal keeps every change: who, what, when, before and after.
points.2: “Undo this change” puts the site back as it was, even after a deletion or a merge of duplicates.
points.3: If a later change touches the same items, undo that one first.

points.1: French is the reference; a missing translation falls back on French.
points.2: The Translations screen shows French, English and German side by side, and what is left to translate or review.
points.3: A machine-suggested translation stays “to review” until you approve it.

points.1: Import and export: the tree as GEDCOM, spreadsheets (people, places, events) and a full backup. Keep a copy from time to time.
points.2: Once the site is online, the database is also backed up every night, automatically.

armsPage.title: Arms and branches
armsPage.intro: Coats of arms tell the family’s story in pictures: where it comes from, whom it married into, how it divided into branches.

explainer.title: The arms, step by step
explainer.intro: A few words of heraldry are enough to read a shield. Here they are, one after the other.

field.title: A field argent
field.body: It all starts with the shield and the colour of its field. Here the field is <argent>argent</argent>: white.

fasces.title: Three bars gules
fasces.body: Then come three <fasce>bars</fasce>, horizontal bands, <gueules>gules</gueules>, that is, red. These are the arms of Croÿ.

quartered.title: Quartered with Renty
quartered.body: A <ecartele>quartered</ecartele> shield is divided into four. In the 1st and 4th quarters, Croÿ; in the 2nd and 3rd, Renty: three <doloire>axe heads</doloire>, the upper two back to back.

stories.intro: What the family tells itself: battles and embassies, weddings, journeys and everyday memories. Each story leads to the people it mentions.

contribute.title: The site is built with the family
contribute.intro: A date to correct, a forgotten ancestor, a photo in a drawer, a story told over dinner: everything you know can enrich the shared history.

how.title: How it works
how.oneBody: A correction, a person, a place, an event, a photo or a story, with its source if you have it.
how.twoBody: Nothing changes on the site before it has been read. They may answer you with a word.
how.threeBody: You are told by email, and your contribution takes its place in the tree and the pages.

signedOut.title: Are you family?
signedOut.body: To propose something, you need family access. Ask for it below: an administrator will answer you.
